title: Joystick Mouse Control
description: Steer your computer's mouse with a joystick; one button turns it on, another clicks.

steps.clip: You need: an Arduino Leonardo and its USB cable, a breadboard, 1 × analog joystick module, 2 × pushbutton, 2 × 10 kΩ resistor, 1 × 220 Ω resistor, 1 × LED, and some jumper wires.
Push the joystick in, its five pins in five columns.
hints: Its pin names are printed next to the pins.
steps.goal: Put the joystick on the breadboard.

steps.clip:
Two wires:
1. The Arduino's 5V pin → the red + row at the bottom of the breadboard.
2. The joystick's VCC pin → that same row.
hints: Power first: + to 5V, − to GND.

steps.clip:
Two wires:
1. The Arduino's GND pin → the blue − row at the bottom of the breadboard.
2. The joystick's GND pin → that same row.
hints: GND is the minus side.

steps.clip: Run a wire from the joystick's HORZ pin to A0 on the Arduino.
hints: A0 is on the Arduino's ANALOG IN side.

steps.clip: Run a wire from the joystick's VERT pin to A1 on the Arduino.
hints: A1 is on the Arduino's ANALOG IN side.

steps.clip: Push the On/Off button in across the middle gap: two legs above the gap, two below.
hints: The two legs in one column (above and below the gap) are always joined inside the button.
Pressing joins the left column to the right column.
steps.goal: Put the On/Off button across the middle gap.

steps.clip: Run a wire from the On/Off button's left column (top half) to pin 2 on the Arduino.
hints: Any hole in that column works.
Pin 2 is on the Arduino's row of numbered sockets.
steps.goal: Connect one side of the On/Off button to pin 2.

steps.clip: Run a wire from the On/Off button's right column (bottom half) to the red + row.
hints: When you press, 5V flows through the button to the pin.
steps.goal: Connect the other side of the On/Off button to 5V.

steps.clip: Push a 10 kΩ resistor in: one leg in the On/Off button's left column (bottom half), the other leg in an empty column.
hints: This is a pull-down: it keeps the pin LOW until you press.
Without it the pin 'floats' and reads random values.
steps.goal: Put a 10 kΩ resistor on the On/Off button's pin side.

steps.clip: Run a wire from the 10 kΩ resistor's other leg to the blue − row.
hints: Now the pin reads LOW, and HIGH only while you press.
steps.goal: Connect the pull-down resistor to GND.

steps.clip: Push the Click button in across the middle gap: two legs above the gap, two below.
hints: The two legs in one column (above and below the gap) are always joined inside the button.
Pressing joins the left column to the right column.
steps.goal: Put the Click button across the middle gap.

steps.clip: Run a wire from the Click button's left column (top half) to pin 3 on the Arduino.
hints: Any hole in that column works.
Pin 3 is on the Arduino's row of numbered sockets.
steps.goal: Connect one side of the Click button to pin 3.

steps.clip: Run a wire from the Click button's right column (bottom half) to the red + row.
hints: When you press, 5V flows through the button to the pin.
steps.goal: Connect the other side of the Click button to 5V.

steps.clip: Push a 10 kΩ resistor in: one leg in the Click button's left column (bottom half), the other leg in an empty column.
hints: This is a pull-down: it keeps the pin LOW until you press.
Without it the pin 'floats' and reads random values.
steps.goal: Put a 10 kΩ resistor on the Click button's pin side.

steps.clip: Run a wire from the 10 kΩ resistor's other leg to the blue − row.
hints: Now the pin reads LOW, and HIGH only while you press.
steps.goal: Connect the pull-down resistor to GND.

steps.clip: Push a 220 Ω resistor into the breadboard. Put its two legs in two different columns.
hints: A resistor works either way round.
It protects the LED — without it the LED can burn out.
steps.goal: Put the resistor for the LED on the breadboard.

steps.clip: Run a wire from one leg of the 220 Ω resistor to pin 5 on the Arduino.
hints: Put the wire in any hole in the same column as the leg. Use exactly this pin — the code counts through the pins in order.
Pin 5 is on the Arduino's row of numbered sockets.

steps.clip: Put the LED in: the long leg in the same column as the 220 Ω resistor's other leg, the short leg in the next column.
hints: The long leg is + (the anode). Backwards, the LED stays dark.
Legs in the same column are connected — no wire needed.
steps.goal: Connect the LED's long leg (+) to the resistor.

steps.clip: Run a wire from the LED's short leg to the blue − row.
hints: The short leg is − (the cathode).
GND is the minus side of the circuit.
steps.goal: Connect the LED's short leg (−) to GND.

steps.clip: Copy the code into the Arduino IDE and click Upload. Press the On/Off button (the LED lights), then push the joystick: the mouse pointer moves. The other button clicks.
